kjv: Why callest thou me (Jesus) good? there is none good but one, that is, God
mine: Why do you ask me (Jesus) about what is good? There is only one who is good
note: TR "ti me legeis agathon; oudeis agathos ei me heis ho theos" assimilates to Mark 10:18/Luke 18:19; Sinaiticus and Vaticanus have Matthew's distinctive "ti me erotas peri tou agathou; heis estin ho agathos".

kjv: Good Master, what good thing shall I do
mine: Teacher, what good deed must I do
note: TR adds "agathe" ("good") to "Teacher" from Mark/Luke; absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus, matching Matthew's reworded reply in 19:17.

mine: in the renewal of all things
note: palingenesia here is the cosmic renewal of the world at the end (as in Stoic and Jewish usage), not the individual spiritual "regeneration" of Titus 3:5 that the English word now suggests.
